entry.title: Black Belt Eagle Scout Shares New Song “Fantasy”
entry.summary: The Swinomish musician enlisted her family members to join her in its music video
entry.content:
Black Belt Eagle Scout has returned with “Fantasy,” her first new song in three years. In that time, the Swinomish musician Katherine “KP” Paul was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, struggled to walk, and lost the ability to play guitar. “Fantasy” delves into the stresses and struggles of a capitalistic society, and how it took a toll on her body. The single also comes with a music video directed by her cousin Priscilla Hensley and Evan Benally Atwood that features Paul’s mother, aunt, and relatives as dancers wearing handmade Iñupiat garments. You can watch it below.

“I wrote ‘Fantasy’ during a time in my life when I was transitioning out of the nonprofit world and into making music full time,” explains Paul. “I was feeling really burnt out and disconnected from the work I was doing. Working in the Native nonprofit world, I often felt this pressure to be some kind of superwoman representing Native people, while also trying to fit into systems that didn't always reflect who we are as Native people. I was at a point where I didn't want to keep trying to fit into something that didn't feel right for me anymore. I wanted to make music, feel free, spend time in the trees, and reconnect with myself outside of all those expectations.”

Black Belt Eagle Scout released her latest LP, The Land, the Water, the Sky, in early 2023, and toured heavily in support of it before she abruptly had to stop performing due to her health issues.

Revisit the Rising interview Black Belt Eagle Scout Is Bringing Queer Indigenous Stories to Indie Rock.

entry.title: A Supreme Elliott Smith Collection? What the Hell, Sure
entry.summary: The streetwear brand is launching a capsule collection inspired by the late songwriter
entry.content:
When it was My Bloody Valentine, we stood by. When it was Daniel Johnston, we bit our tongues. But Elliott Smith—that’s a bridge too far. Streetwear brand Supreme has a long history of collaborations with musicians both living and dead, to various degrees of bad taste. Their latest is a capsule collection inspired by the late songwriter, who took his own life in 2003. At least Supreme got the permission of Smith’s estate.

The Supreme x Elliott Smith collection officially launches November 12; for now, you can check out a photo gallery of the clothes, which include t-shirts and sweatshirts emblazoned with the covers for Figure 8, Either/Or, and Elliott Smith. “None of the designs are that good either,” says Chris Panicker, Pitchfork’s in-house designer.

Read more about Either/Or, Smith’s 1997 opus, at No. 4 in Pitchfork’s brand-new list of The 100 Best Indie Rock Albums of All Time.

entry.title: YouTube Squashes Feud With Billboard Charts
entry.summary: A year after the company said it would no longer submit its numbers for chart consideration, it’s reversed course
entry.content:
In 2025, YouTube announced it would no longer submit its streams for Billboard consideration, due to the company’s decision to weigh subscriber streams more favorably than ones on the platform’s free, ad-supported tier. At the time, Lyor Cohen, YouTube’s global head of music, referred to the change as an “outdated formula” that “ignores the massive engagement from fans who don’t have a subscription.” Well forget all of that, because YouTube has reversed course.

“We are returning to the Billboard charts starting in 2027,” Cohen wrote in an updated note to his original blog. “Billboard’s new methodology better reflects how fans engage with music today across both subscription and ad-supported services.” As Coen notes, Billboard recently cut down the ratio of streams between the subscriber and ad-supported tiers from 1:2.5 to 1:1.5 (in other words, now one subscriber stream counts as much as one-and-a-half ad-supported streams, rather than the previous two and a half). The change takes effect on January 16.

It’s unclear why YouTube was down with the soon-to-be-updated radio rather than the 1:1 Cohen initially hinted at in his first post. We’ve asked the company’s reps for comment. Until then, stan accounts are now free to include YouTube again in their attempts to push their faves up the Billboard 200.

entry.title: New Order Plot 2027 U.S. Tour
entry.summary: Future Islands will support the synth-pop greats on three Texas dates to launch the Southern run
entry.content:
New Order will race through the South on a brief U.S. tour in March 2027. The stint kicks off with a trio of Texas dates—in Austin, Fort Worth, and Houston—before the band heads to New Orleans, Nashville, and Miami. They will be performing with stand-ins for the eminent husband-and-wife duo of Gillian Gilbert and Stephen Morris, as Gilbert receives treatment for cancer. See all the band’s forthcoming tour dates, including an imminent South American stint, below. Future Islands, Zachery Allan Starkey, and DJ Arthur Baker are supporting the U.S. dates.

Before the South American slate, New Order are set to attend this year’s Rock Hall ceremony; Bernard Sumner will also be representing Joy Division for the bands’ joint induction.

entry.title: GTA VI Is Putting on a Music Festival
entry.summary: Sure, why not
entry.content:
Not content with securing an original Justice score, anything-goes soundtrack, and bundle of superstar-curated radio stations, Rockstar Games has announced Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival. Coming to Miami’s premier convention center, Mana Wynwood, on the alarmingly near date of November 21, the one-dayer is set to be headlined by Travis Scott and friends (billed as Cactus Jack), Cardi B, and CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso. Sets from Justice and Metro Boomin take second billing, alongside an undercard that includes local boy Nick León playing back to back with DJ Python. Take a look at the poster below and stay tuned for further enterprises from our GTA VI overlords.

Don Toliver, Kodak Black, and Sofaygo will join Scott for the Cactus Jack headliner, while Rauw Alejandro will bring along some surprise guests for another spin on the posse set. Fellow Puerto Rican Tainy is also on the bill, along with two more back-to-back DJ sets: the Dare B2B Fcukers and Prospa B2B Skream. Suero, the collaborative project of Jubilee, Berrakka, and Jonny From Space, complete the bill.

entry.title: Rosalía Celebrates Lux Anniversary with 1,000-Song Playlist
entry.summary: Featuring Mozart, Yung Lean, Labi Siffre, and Pink Floyd
entry.content:
Yesterday marked a full calendar year since Rosalía dropped her third album Lux, and she marked the occasion with a couple of celebratory offerings. They include a 1,000-song Spotify playlist titled “1000 TEMAS QUE TE DAN LUX,” with tracks from Kate Bush, Mozart, Bon Iver, Yung Lean, Labi Siffre, Pink Floyd, Caetano Veloso, Verdi, and many more. Give it a spin below.

Rosalía also rang in Lux’s first birthday with the release of a limited-edition vinyl box set and, in true modern pop auteur fashion, a Substack post. In the letter, written in Spanish, Rosalía reflected on the creation of the album and her past year, which she describes as “one of the hardest of my life, but also one of the most meaningful.”

“I love acts of service; there’s something about preparing something for someone else that fascinates me,” she wrote. “That’s why I made a playlist of 1,000 songs I listened to during the years I dreamed up, composed and shared Lux.”

Since introducing Lux to the world last year, Rosalía has barely taken a breather. She supported the album on a critically-acclaimed tour; sang “Reliquía” en pointe on Saturday Night Live; and released a song with Fontaines D.C. On November 12, she’ll perform at the Latin Grammys, where she and Lux are up for seven awards including Album and Record of the Year.

entry.title: Hayley Williams Hangs in Her Hotel Room in “Dream Girl in Shibuya” Video
entry.summary: The Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party track just got a black-and-white visual to match
entry.content:
Oh, to spend an evening lounging in a hotel bed with Hayley Williams while she noodles on the guitar. That’s essentially the premise of the music video for “Dream Girl in Shibuya,” a song from Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party that’s all about hoping someone will come hit up your hotel room. Check out the black-and-white clip, which was filmed by Zachary Gray, below.

Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party, which dropped in 2025, marked Williams’ third solo album and first independent release. She’s currently in the midst of her second tour of the year in support of the record, which will head to Brazil and a few other South American cities later this month. Somehow, she also found time this year to launch a new project, Power Snatch, with Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party’s producer Daniel James. Her band Paramore’s most recent album, This Is Why, came out in 2023.

entry.title: Watch the Strokes Play “Lonely in the Future” and “Going Shopping” on SNL
entry.summary: Nick Valensi didn’t join, but Walton Goggins did
entry.content:
The Strokes dropped by Saturday Night Live last night to perform songs from their latest album Reality Awaits alongside first-time host Druski. Still sans longtime guitarist Nick Valensi, the band performed “Lonely in the Future” and “Going Shopping.” Walton Goggins, the star of the latter song‘s music video, joined in on the bongos when they played it. Watch both performances below.

Last night’s set marked the New York group’s fifth time on SNL. They last featured on the show six years ago, behind their 2020 album The New Abnormal. This time around, their performance arrived on the tail of North American and European legs of their Reality Awaits tour, which will bring them to Mexico, South America, and Australia in the coming months. Openers have included Thundercat, the Walkmen’s Hamilton Leithauser, and Cage the Elephant.

The Strokes followed up their SNL spot by releasing an official music video for “Lonely in the Future.” Directed by Warren Fu, the clip uses puppets to depict a number of familiar faces, from artists Lou Reed and Bach to controversial billionaires like Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, and Mark Zuckerberg. (Bezos and Musk even have a love story subplot.)

Revisit Eric Harvey’s review of Reality Awaits.

entry.title: Richard Lloyd, Television Guitarist, Dies at 75
entry.summary: Lloyd co-founded the pioneering rock band alongside Tom Verlaine, Billy Ficca, and Richard Hell
entry.content:
Richard Lloyd, the co-founding guitarist of Television, has died, The New York Times reports. The cause was cholangiocarcinoma, a bile duct cancer. He was 75. In August, a GoFundMe was launched to raise money for Lloyd’s treatment. “His loving wife Sheila and his dog Willie Mays were with him at the end,” his family said in a statement to Rolling Stone.

Television formed in 1973 after Tom Verlaine, Richard Hell, and Billy Ficca ended their first band, the Neon Boys, and recruited Lloyd as a second guitarist. Part of a pioneering wave of New York City punk acts, Television built a cult following at local mainstays Max’s Kansas City and CBGB. The band’s sound—grounded in the driving, elaborate guitar interplay between Verlaine and Lloyd—was a sharp detour from their contemporaries’ three-chord melodies. After signing to Elektra in 1977, Television released the seminal Marquee Moon and, a year later, sophomore effort Adventure, before tensions between Verlaine and Lloyd led to the group’s breakup.

“Richard Lloyd chisels notes out hard while Verlaine works with a subtle twang and a trace of space-gazing delirium,” Chris Dahlen wrote in Pitchfork’s review of Marquee Moon and Adventure. “They play lines that are stately and chiming, rutting and torrential, the riff, the solo, the rare power chord, and most of all, the power note.”

Richard Lloyd was born Richard John Alt in 1951 in Pittsburgh. Following his parents split, his mother remarried and moved the family to Greenwich Village. Lloyd began playing the guitar at the age of seven after spotting one at a cousin’s sleepover. “I recognized that the guitar was their magic wand,” Lloyd told Guitar World in January, about his early encounters with Beatles’ records. “They were casting a spell over young people. It’s an impulse that never left me.”

After brief stints in Boston and Los Angeles, Lloyd moved back to New York in his early twenties, where he first encountered Verlaine and Hell. “We were ahead of the curve,” Lloyd told KEXP in 2017, of his time playing in Television. “Marquee Moon still sells—it's never been out of print. And it’s still on top records of all time lists, which makes me proud and happy.” Television returned for one final LP, Television, in 1992. Verlaine died in 2023 following a brief illness.

After Television’s initial disbandment, Lloyd went on to have a prolific solo career, releasing nine albums and contributing guitar to records by Matthew Sweet, Stephan Eicher, and John Doe of X.

“For many years I wouldn’t touch Television songs,” Lloyd added in this year’s Guitar World interview. “But as the last functioning member of the band, I have a responsibility to the fans. I play a number of Television songs, my own songs, and some covers, so everybody has a good time.”

entry.title: Nick Cave Launches 2027 Tour
entry.summary: Conversations with Nick Cave: An Evening of Talk & Music will combine a Q&A with live performance
entry.content:
Nick Cave is heading out on the road next year, reviving the format of his 2019 tour blending a Q&A, live performance, and career retrospective. The 2027 edition of Conversations with Nick Cave: An Evening of Talk & Music kicks off in Vancouver next April, and will traverse North America before concluding in New Orleans in May. Check out a full itinerary below.

The new tour is presented by the Red Hand Files, an online correspondence platform Cave launched in 2018 where fans can send him questions. Over the years, he’s become known for his unfiltered and thoughtful answers to any question that comes through.

“The Red Hand Files have grown in reach and stature; the topics of conversation have broadened, and it feels like the right time to return to America, a different America from eight years ago, and bring the Conversations… show back,” Cave shared in press materials. “I’ll have my piano with me, play some songs, and answer questions. What could possibly go wrong?”

Elsewhere this year, Cave earned an Oscar nomination for Best Original Song for “Train Dreams,” which he wrote with Bryce Dessner for the film of the same name. In August, he also put on a large-scale hometown concert in Brighton and invited fellow Aussie Kylie Minogue onstage as a special guest.

entry.title: Macklemore Accuses U.S. Arenas of Turning Down Free Palestine Tour
entry.summary: “Once they realized these were my benefit shows for Palestine, those dates were suddenly off the table”
entry.content:
When Macklemore announced his Free Palestine Tour—a run of benefit shows in Dublin, London, and Paris following his removal as Ed Sheeran’s opener —he promised U.S. dates were not far behind. But Stateside arenas, like their football stadium counterparts, are apparently less than enthused to book the rapper over his pro-Palestine comments. In a statement posted to Instagram on November 6, Macklemore accused nine venues of not allowing the tour to move forward.

“We received available dates at these arenas through the end of the year. But once they found out these were my benefit shows for Palestine, those dates were suddenly off the table,” he wrote. “The doors were closed. The conversations were all different, but the result was the same. These shows were not going to be allowed to happen in these venues. In over twenty years of touring, I’ve never experienced anything like this.”

The arenas Macklemore named were Madison Square Garden, Prudential Center. Barclays Center, UBS Arena, Intuit Dome, Kia Forum, Crypto.com Arena, Chase Center, and Climate Pledge Arena. Pitchfork has reached out to representatives at each venue for comment.

“I’m three years past giving two shits about maintaining any relationships, business or personal, with anyone that isn’t riding for a Free Palestine,” the rapper added, noting that he will continue to look for spaces to perform. “I’d rather lose every opportunity in this industry than spend another day protecting people who value their business relationships with Israel more than they value Palestinian human life.”

You can read his full statement below.

Ed Sheeran Attempts to Clarify Gaza Stance, Again Blames Venues for Kicking Macklemore Off Tour

In over twenty years of touring, I’ve never experienced anything like this.

But this is not an isolated incident. For decades, activists, poets, writers, musicians and entertainers who have stood in solidarity with the Palestinian people have faced consequences for doing so. Many have paid a far greater price than I have.

Looking back over the last three years, the only real regret I have is not speaking publicly when Zionists were kicking me under the table. At the time, I didn’t believe that centering what was happening to me was worth taking any attention away from the genocide in Palestine.

But the intimidation, manipulation and suppression I experienced are part of how those in power keep entertainers quiet. It’s their main tactic to keep us in line. Shut up and dribble, or you will be punished.

But at this point, I’m three years past giving two shits about maintaining any relationships, business or personal, with anyone that isn’t riding for a Free Palestine.

I’d rather lose every opportunity in this industry than spend another day protecting people who value their business relationships with Israel more than they value Palestinian human life.

We live in a country that prides itself on freedom of speech. Yet we’ve reached a point where a handful of billionaires can decide which causes are acceptable, which voices are welcome and which human lives are worth defending.

Today it’s Palestine. What will it be tomorrow?

To these owners, the words Free Palestine represent a threat. Not because they endanger anyone, but because those words challenge the systems of power they have built their fortunes on.

The tides are turning. Just three nights ago, Abdul El-Sayed won his Senate race on a platform that included ending the genocide in Gaza and stopping U.S. arms sales to Israel. AIPAC spent $42 million trying to defeat him. And they still couldn’t win.

The trouble with buying power is believing you’ve bought the people too.

The billionaires depend on our silence and complicity. They forget that we buy their tickets. We fill their arenas. We build their empires. And we have the power to bring them down.

The people have spoken. We want an end to the genocide and we want a Free Palestine. The arenas have made their decision. Now we’ll make ours. If they think the threat of never playing another arena in America will make me retreat into silence, they got me fucked up.

There will be more shows for Palestine. We’ll keep working with other artists and organizers, continuing where we left off in Europe. We’ll probably just take that shit outside where it belonged in the first place.

Our commitment to raising funds and standing in solidarity with the Palestinian people remains the same.

There comes a point when the world changes, not because those in power give us permission, but because the people stop asking for it.

We build our own stages.

They may own the arenas. But they do not own the people who fill them. And they never will.

FREE PALESTINE 🇵🇸❤️✨

entry.title: Cleo Reed Announces New EP Is This How Empires Die?
entry.summary: Watch the music video for “American Dream,” filmed in Oklahoma on the Fourth of July
entry.content:
The political and socioeconomic issues that Cleo Reed sang about on their 2025 album Cuntry are still plaguing the U.S. In an upcoming EP Is This How Empires Die?, the musician continues to examine the life of queer and working class individuals in America. The record, out December 4, includes lead single “American Dream” and its accompanying video, filmed at the Demery Family Rodeo in Oklahoma on the Fourth of July. In it, Reed questions American policy, surveillance, and patriotism across a landscape that juxtaposes scenes of Black youth playing with closing shots of the singer’s silhouette backdropped by flames. Watch it below.

“‘American Dream’ is my anti-anthem, like the panic after waking up from a bad dream in a cold sweat,” Reed explained in a press statement. “It’s afro-surrealist. It’s anti-imperial. I took on the daunting task and now we’re here! The age of AI-music, mass flooding, surveillance, and crisis–somehow interrupted by the occasional joys of traditional holidays. I wrote the song for the hypothetical day when I’m celebrating the 4th of July and then the storm comes. This is a moment of waking from the perfect dream. Face reality.”

entry.title: Angine de Poitrine Beam in Third Member
entry.summary: They appeared on stage to play the triangle
entry.content:
On Thursday, the buzzy, anonymous, polka-dotted duo Angine de Poitrine briefly became a three-piece, when a similarly dressed third member shuffled on stage with a triangle to accompany entities Khn and Klek on a new song. Whether this unnamed individual plans on joining the group permanently is still unknown (both to fans and, apparently, their publicist, who tells Pitchfork they aren’t sure either). I do hope it happens, though; as you can see in the video below, they play a mean triangle.

Angine de Poitrine are currently wrapping up a run of live dates through North America. They’ll then power down for a few months before heading out on a 2027 international trek.

If you’re still confused about this whole Angine thing, check out Christopher R. Weingarten’s review of the group’s latest album.

entry.title: Future, Drake, and Travis Scott Join Forces for “Ya Hit”
entry.summary: Loe Shimmy also features on the first song from Future’s new album
entry.content:
Six months after his murky inquiry into truth and persona on The Real Me, Future has brought along some pals to launch a new phase. “Ya Hit,” billed as the first official song from a forthcoming album, features Drake, Travis Scott, and Florida rapper Loe Shimmy, trading verses over an ATL Jacob beat, with adlibs from Sexyy Red. Check it out below, along with Jim Joe & Lewy’s cover art.

Details of that new Future LP are scarce, but he appears to be launching straight in with the momentum from its predecessor. As he prepares to headline Camp Flog Gnaw in Los Angeles, he hinted at more activity with an X post this week that read, “Bringin the static back #INFINITY.” The new song is Future and Drake’s second collaboration of the year—after the Iceman cut “Ran to Atlanta”—and Drake’s first with Scott since 2023’s “Meltdown.”

entry.title: 10 New Albums You Should Listen to Now: Twisted Teens, Bassvictim, and More
entry.summary: Stream new releases from Twisted Teens, Bassvictim, Oso Oso, and Lil Baby
entry.content:
With so much good music being released all the time, it can be hard to determine what to listen to first. Every week, Pitchfork offers a run-down of significant new drops available on streaming services. This week’s batch includes new albums from Twisted Teens, Bassvictim, Shygirl, and more. Subscribe to Pitchfork’s New Music Friday newsletter to get our recommendations in your inbox every week. (All releases featured here are independently selected by our editors. When you buy something through our affiliate links, however, Pitchfork earns an affiliate commission.)

Twisted Teens: The Holy Cross Tigers [Sub Pop]

Focusing on Twisted Teens’ relentless output in 2026 misses the point. Instead, track the fluidity of their strut through garage rock, country, and traditional folk; on The Holy Cross Tigers, that effortless sway of hypnotic steel guitar over shuffling drums presents like an old jukebox standard that you’re hearing for the first time. Place your trust in that timelessness. Caspian Hollywell and RJ Santos steer their New Orleans band like a pontoon boat: balanced, unadorned, and old-school in that it reinforces only the bare-bones necessities required for a good time.

Bassvictim: Peace + War [Warner]

Bassvictim’s electroclash brings the lopsided, derelict genre to a new audience with all of the mess and less of the sex. Vocalist Maria Manow flips between feeling happy and sad, then fat and skinny, on “Happysad,” while she admits to feeling shit when she wakes up over the crushed-up industrial beats of “Wake Up.” The album’s production scuttles from laptop twee and bloghouse to freewheeling experimentations like “No. 33 piano,” which wobbles through febrile piano loops.

Shygirl: Swallow! [Because]

There’s a reason that time-honored rave aphorism “PLUR” has an L: even the staunchest club kids need love, too. London scene veteran Shygirl’s latest album, inspired by a blossoming relationship, relishes in that sweet spot between dancefloor deliverance and dream-pop catharsis, drawing as much on Miss Kittin and Mazzy Star. Reuniting with Club Shy co-producer Karma Kid and bringing in Oklou’s right-hand man Casey MQ, Shy unfurls a clean record that’s sultry and soft in equal measure, like any romance worth its salt.

Lil Baby: Fresh [Quality Control/Motown]

Since he dropped his debut studio LP on Quality Control in 2018, Lil Baby has kept his sound local, staying loyal to melodic trap and a close-knit crew of producers from the region. His new album, Fresh, tests that hometown devotion out on poppier songs, including his first collaboration with Pharrell. Features from Future and Young Thug—the only guests on the album save labelmate Rylo Rodriguez—basically spell out the crossover Baby's looking to emulate. “If I can’t make hits,” he told the New York Times’ Popcast last week, “I ain’t gonna make music no more.” (Lucky for him, the lead single “Dead Fresh” just became his first Top 40 single since 2022.)

Sufjan Stevens: Worst Christmas Ever! [Asthmatic Kitty]

When the holiday season rolls around, Sufjan Stevens is all-in on cover songs and original tracks to deck the halls. What originally took shape as Songs for Christmas, Vols. 1-5 in 2006 eventually led to the 2012 box set Silver & Gold, featuring dozens of new songs alongside the old material. Stevens’ commitment to Christmas cheer is extensive, to say the least. That’s why he’s now compiled Worst Christmas Ever!, which distills those holiday hits and fan favorites from his Christmas catalog into a single collection. Already know “Sister Winter” and “Put the Lights on the Tree” like the back of your wreath? Fret not, for there’s a special present tucked away just for you: the new original song “On This Christmas (It Only Gets Better).”

Skepta: The Fork and Knife [Epic]

Skepta hasn’t dropped a full-length solo project since 2019 but the grime star has stayed plenty busy, collaborating with Fred Again.. an EP, pulling up for a surprise set at Glastonbury, and releasing more than a dozen singles—including new tracks “Pandora’s Box” and “Gas Me Up (Dilligent),” which detail the ups and downs of success. The Fork and Knife might be Skepta’s first album in seven years, but the North London MC treats it like he has nothing to prove.

Daine: In Endless Awe & Agony [Pack/Create]

At the tender age of 23, the Australian singer-songwriter Daine has already lived a few different musical lives, from teenaged emo pop-rap offerings (now relegated to YouTube) to a requisite hyperpop baddie era. Next is their debut studio release In Endless Awe & Agony, which leans into the unfiltered texture of their voice. The record, Daine’s first project sans Auto-Tune, is an introduction to their feathery mezzo-soprano. But it also reaches for bigger pop hooks in the lineage of mid-2010s acts like Passion Pit and the Naked and the Famous.

Oso Oso: An Exchange of Information [Feral Twin]

Six albums into their basement-platinum emo-pop project, Long Island’s Oso Oso are their own blueprint. An Exchange of Information, the follow-up to 2024’s Life Till Bones, marks the inaugural release on Hop Along drummer Mark Quinlan’s new label. Turns out, you take yourself wherever you go: the new project harkens all the way back to Oso Oso’s 2015 debut, ripping into familiar territory with fresh energy. Led by singer-songwriter Jade Lilitri, the band closes out an indie-rock walkabout with a rediscovered passion for the head-banging pop punk that brought bristle to their earlier work.

Sam Gendel: Advanced White Trash [self-released]

If you’ve heard Sam Gendel’s jazz-forward albums like The Room, Cookup, and Audiobook, you might be surprised by his latest, Advanced White Trash. The album mostly abandons the saxophone, the instrument Gendel is known for, instead opting for Auto-Tuned rap, glitchy R&B, and corroded 808s. Partly inspired by the hours of YouTube the musician has watched, it’s the sound of brainrot with pockets, like the mellifluous “Pattern Dance,” reminiscent of his colorful acoustic work.

Untitled (halo): Untitled (halo) [Dirty Hit]

Untitled (Halo) is a band born out of “lack of a scene or music in LA.” The group of Ariana Mamnoon, Jack Dione, Jay Are, and Nicholas Noneman have set to carve out a DIY space in Los Angeles through their party series, and now with their debut album. Untitled (halo) is likely to draw comparisons to Bar Italia, while their occasional Auto-Tuned whispers might remind listeners of Chanel Beads. But the band has plenty more to offer, like bloghouse (“Sex”), trip-hop (“Thief”), and indie pop (“Easy Rider”).

entry.title: Watch Slayyyter Date a Skeleton in New “Hey Boyyy” Video
entry.summary: Including a romantic excursion on the Seine
entry.content:
Slayyyter’s next album, Wor$t Man in America, is inching closer by the minute, and she’s been generous with her output since announcing the project, giving us several new songs alongside self-directed music videos. She now shares another new track, “Hey Boyyy,” as well as a clip that follows the pop star around Hollywood and Paris while she sings about an exhilarating romantic spark.

Earlier this year, Slayyyter performed “Hey Boyyy” as an unreleased single at Wor$t Girl in Nyyyc, a pop-up show at Bushwick’s Market Hotel. The new drop follows the release of Wor$t Man in America singles “Brand New Chanel$,”“Crank 2,” and “I Think He’s Got a Girl.”

Revisit Walden Green‘s profile Saint Slayyyter.

entry.title: Go Fishing With Twisted Teens in Video for “I Spend My Time Crying”
entry.summary: Their new album, The Holy Cross Tigers, is out today
entry.content:
Twisted Teens released their latest album, The Holy Cross Tigers, today on Sub Pop, and they’re celebrating the big day with a music video for its song “I Spend My Time Crying.” It’s another visual stunner courtesy of Jack Massucci, the same director behind the band’s “Florida Water Blues” video. In it, a young kid traverses New Orleans to fish, goes door to door selling his game, and learns how to drive, among other things. A certain calico guinea pig makes an appearance, too. Watch the video below.

The Holy Cross Tigers is Twisted Teens’ third full-length LP of 2026. It follows January’s Blame the Clown and July’s Florida Water Blues, as well as their 2024 debut self-titled album. “I Spend My Time Crying” takes a different route compared to “Stalks” and “When We First Met,” downshifting into a more acoustic guitar-driven sway.

Twisted Teens are currently on tour through the end of the year. Once they wrap up this leg opening for Kurt Vile and the Violators, they fly to Australia for their own run of shows as headliners. In 2027, the band will perform at a handful of high-profile festivals, too, including Primavera Sound in Barcelona and Best Kept Secret in the Netherlands.

Read Nina Corcoran’s profile on the band, Twisted Teens Hit the Big Time.

entry.title: Listen to Olivia Rodrigo’s New Song “Take Me Home (4 Christmas)”
entry.summary: "I'm so thoughtful and merry and kind, and I was waiting a really long time"
entry.content:
All Olivia Rodrigo wants for Christmas is for her partner’s grandma to think she’s cool. Rodrigo just shared her first holiday song, aptly titled “Take Me Home (4 Christmas),” and it’s all about that first time you meet your honey’s extended family on their turf. Written with usual suspects Dan Nigro and Amy Allen, it’s accompanied by a music video starring Saturday Night Live’s Ben Marshall as Rodrigo’s boo, and Cynthia Nixon as his mom. Watch it below.

“Take Me Home” is Rodrigo’s follow-up to the David Byrne-starring video for her “Expectations” remix with tourmate Chappell Roan. Both songs featured on her 2026 album You Seem Pretty Sad For a Girl So in Love, which she’s currently bringing around the world on the Unraveled Tour. Her opening lineup features Grace Ives, Wolf Alice, Devon Again, the Last Dinner Party, and Die Spitz.

Earlier this year, Rodrigo also launched her own benefit music festival, Daisy Chain Fields. The inaugural edition, which took place in California in August and was inspired by Lilith Fair, gathered an age-diverse lineup of female artists from Quiet Light to the Breeders. At the even, which raised $20 million for sponsors like Planned Parenthood and Center for Reproductive Rights, Rodrigo also debuted a new song inspired by The Handmaids Tale, “Serena Joy.”

entry.title: Toro y Moi Reveals New Album Unusua
entry.summary: The project, which quietly appeared on Chaz Bear’s Bandcamp page, drops this month
entry.content:
In October, Toro y Moi premiered the supposedly one-off, piano-driven single “Proof.” Turns out it’s part of a new self-produced album called Unusua. Not much is known about the seven-track LP, which quietly appeared on Chaz Bear’s Bandcamp page in recent days, but Pitchfork has confirmed it’s out November 20. You can listen to “Proof” below.

Earlier this year, Toro y Moi released an acoustic version of his 2025 album Hole Erth and opened for Haruomi Hosono on the latter’s Stateside dates.
